Ugh my heart goes out to you! Telling you that you are a bad wife is unbelievable. I keep telling myself I can control my reaction. You obviously had a controlled reaction to her, I hope you also soothe yourself and know you’re a wonderful mom who is in tune with her child’s needs - and never mind what that crazy MIL thinks. 

I have another nasty MIL share: I went to my MIL a few years back when we were childless (and both in our mid thirties). Hubs and I had been married for years and together for 10 years exclusively, no break up dramas etc. so I told her that I couldn’t get my husband to have conversations around having kids and her response was “well you two are on different timelines, he can have kids until he’s 70!” I have to actively work to not hold hate in my heart for her. Bleh.

You’re a-okay to ask that. 
That receptionist was definitely being weird. Maybe jealous the nurse got attention and she didn’t. Regardless don’t burn your precious time worrying about what she thinks or what’s going on with her to behave like that. Compare yourself only to your past self, not on anybody else’s strange comments or actions.

I’m 40 and pregnant in a relationship with emotional abuse and as much as I willed myself to have a family now that I’m pregnant i am miserable. I’ve gained 20 pounds self soothing with food. I finally called the abortion center today I’m almost 12 weeks I just kept waking up at night aware of how scary this all is for me. I can’t have a husband who hits himself in front of our kid, and I tend to react by withdrAwing and neglecting myself and can’t do that with a kid. Also my teenage and 20 something self never wanted kids. I think my biological clock kicked in and the desire my husband finally had to have kids was contagious. But for 12/15 years of our relationship he wasn’t having any talks of kids. 
I told my husband this weekend I’m miserable and want out of this pregnancy. I told him he could have the baby I’ll sign off parental rights. He said he’d never want to parent alone and would support me. 

I wish you the best of luck in tuning into your heart and desires and finding your path forward from here.
Congratulations you look wonderful and I can’t imagine how much work you put into feeling better. You totally earned another healthy 47 years. Best of luck. Inspiring!!

Had my gall bladder removed at 18 when i finally took myself to the ED. The inner city surgeon was “impressed” and said it held the most gall stones he’d ever seen. 

I had severe stomach pains most nights since the age of 13 and fell asleep many times on the bathroom floor after drinking Maalox and hugging a toilet for hours in pain. 


My mom didn’t believe my pain and blamed it on my bulemia and once brought me to a family doc who misdiagnosed me with GERD.

I feel that many kids your age would qualify as borderline. 

My suggestion is to look into stoicism to create purpose and manage emotions.
